Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility

photocopy noun and verb

also photocopier, copier, make a copy, photocopying

classical

Asin. Poll. ap. Cic. Fam. 10.31.6: tibi eārum exemplar mīsī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 359: exemplar phōtotypicum

exemplar, exemplāris n.

noun, third declension

a copy

A copy of a document, as in Cicero’s letters. Where it matters that a machine made it, Traupman adds phōtotypicum.

Other words

  • dēscrībō, dēscrībere, dēscrīpsī, dēscrīptum — copy, make a copy

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.21 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 359: phōtotypicē dēscrībere

    Lewis & Short: to copy off, transcribe from an original, frequent in Cicero.

  • exemplum phōtotypicum — a photocopy

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. copy: photocopy

  • māchina phōtotypica — a photocopier

    also used · modern · Traupman 359; M-O s.v. copy: photocopier

Examples

  • Duo exemplāria hujus chartae dēscrībe, sīs.

    Make two copies of this page, please.composed

See also scan, original.

SourcesLewis & Short: exemplar · Lewis & Short: describo · Lewis & Short: exemplum · Lewis & Short: machina

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 359, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. copy: photocopy; copy: photocopier.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
